The image is a microscopic view (100 µm scale bar) showing:
- Branched conidiophores with tree-like branching structure
- Dense grape-like clusters of round/ovoid conidia at the tips
- Classic botryose arrangement — conidia borne in clusters on short sterigmata

This is the unmistakable microscopic signature of **Botrytis cinerea** — the causative agent of Gray Mold. The knowledge base describes "spores are light brown-gray on black stalks" and a "dense velvety gray-brown spore mass," consistent with this microscopic view of branched conidiophores bearing clustered conidia.
